interpretation:
Dominance hierarchy: of 30 tugs, 30 entered at least one multi-responder wasp contest over the day. Win rate is unevenly distributed (Gini = 0.175; 0 = every tug wins its contests equally often, 1 = one tug wins them all) -- tug 6 tops the hierarchy at a 30% win rate over 77 contests. This is not arbitrary: the wasp force F = 0.6/(1+d_norm) + 0.3*battery + 0.1*(1-busy) weights proximity 2.0x more heavily than battery and 6.0x more than idle status, so a tug that has already specialised on a pier (low theta there -> it volunteers more often -> it is more often physically close when it volunteers, because VRTM drift sends idle tugs back to their most-specialised pier hub, see Simulation._reposition_target) systematically wins more of the contests it enters. Win-rate inequality and threshold specialisation are therefore two views of the same underlying feedback loop, not two independent phenomena.

Division of labour: the number of piers with zero primary specialists fell from 7 at t=0h to 0 at t=24h (tug-to-pier assignment Gini at t=24h = 0.325). The mechanism is the asymmetric VRTM update: a performer's threshold drops by xi=2 while every other eligible tug's threshold in that region only rises by phi=0.1. Because xi > phi, a single win pulls a tug's threshold down faster than repeated near-misses push it back up, so the first tug to win in a region gets an increasing edge there on every subsequent request -- a positive-feedback (rich-get-richer) mechanism, not something imposed by the environment.
narrative: Over a simulated 24-hour day with ~538 tow requests, replicated across N=6 independent seeds, the decentralized swarm achieved a mean aircraft wait of 228.2 s (95% CI +/-14.9 s) versus 174.1 s for the centralized greedy baseline (+31.0 %), outside the 20 % competitiveness target (Wilcoxon signed-rank p=0.0312, matched-pairs rank-biserial effect size=1.00). The random-assignment floor and centralized-optimal ceiling give this comparison context (see wait_time_comparison.png). Emergent service zones formed: the fleet-wide specialization index rose from 0.000 to 0.103 averaged over seeds. With fixed (non-adaptive) thresholds the mean wait was 234.3 s and final specialization was 0.000 (p=0.0312 vs adaptive), confirming threshold adaptation drives both the zone formation and the performance. Sensitivity analysis identifies 'fleet_size' as the parameter with the largest impact on mean wait (see sensitivity_tornado.png).
